newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says won't accept US link on NTT procurement.
newsitem.headline: Japan says won't accept US link on NTT procurement.

text.p: An official of Japan's Posts and Telecommunications Ministry said on Monday that Tokyo will not discuss renewing Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp's procurement pact with the United States while Washington links the issue with the granting of a telephone licence to NTT in the United States.
"It would be difficult for us to participate in negotiations on (extending) NTT's procurement pact while the two issues are linked," senior ministry adviser Tochi Minami told a news conference.
He said the United States hoped to start the NTT talks around May. The pact, which sets guidelines for NTT's international purchases of equipment, expires in September.
Minami said the U.S. stance violates the spirit of international trade agreements.
The U.S. Federal Communications Commission informed NTT and Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co earlier this month that it would delay granting them licences to provide international phone services.
The U.S. Trade Representative's office has also asked Japan to scrap the 20 percent ceiling on foreign ownership in NTT and KDD by the end of this year.
